acceptance_tests: Move a wall through direct drag and through language “move that wall 150”; both resolve to equivalent typed operation/Transform semantics.
Use Three.js/proxy interaction while OpenCascade exact regeneration is intentionally delayed; pointer feedback remains live and currentness is honest.
Swap the exact provider adapter in a fixture without changing Plasma entity IDs, relations or Transform schemas.
Inject exact-kernel fillet failure: proxy may remain visible, but commit-critical exact status becomes failed/pending and no approximate fillet is silently accepted.
Regenerate a wall/opening and prove hosted-opening identity survives provider topology changes or reports explicit topology ambiguity.
Round-trip a folded fabrication part through an external specialist path and reconcile returned geometry/process constraints without making external body IDs canonical.
EXTEND/TRIM a beam to a semantic wall face using an analytic termination strategy; moving the wall re-evaluates the beam while preserving the semantic target reference.

CONNECT two walls under butt, miter and priority policies; prove the persistent Relation survives exact topology regeneration and that plan representation can suppress unwanted junction lines independently of solid topology.
SPLIT a solid by a plane and preserve both pieces with lineage; prove later keep/delete/classify operations do not require rerunning an ambiguous destructive cut.
Run exact, 1 µm gap, coincident, near-tangent and micro-sliver fixtures through the same resolver; verify bounded tolerance/healing policy and explicit typed failure beyond limits.
Repeat a Boolean/junction edit cycle many times and assert tolerance/topology complexity does not grow unbounded or silently accumulate micro-edges.
Break a persistent face reference deliberately; dependent commit must hold with topology-identity-loss diagnostics rather than rebind by transient face index.

During drag, use a fast proxy at interactive frame rate; on release execute only the affected exact region, mark exact status computing/current explicitly, and publish only after validation/cleanliness checks pass.

composition_examples: WallJunction = CONNECT + EXTEND/TRIM + optional SUBTRACT + SIMPLIFY + persistent wall-wall Relation.
WindowInWall = CONNECT(host) + SUBTRACT(opening volume) + hosted-element Relation + representation rules.
BeamToColumn = CONNECT + EXTEND/TRIM + optional connection-component generation + fabrication Relations.
SplitAndClassify = SPLIT + preserve all pieces + semantic classification/ownership assignment.

interaction_mapping.cut: Must resolve explicitly to TRIM, SPLIT, SUBTRACT, SECTION or another declared semantic operation rather than remaining an ambiguous low-level command.
interaction_mapping.draw/place/push-pull/repeat/attach-host: User-facing interaction verbs may compile to one or more canonical geometry verbs plus Entity/Relation/Transform changes.
interaction_mapping.join: Must resolve explicitly to CONNECT, UNION, MERGE, SEW or an architectural relationship policy; raw geometric coincidence is not sufficient.

canonical_geometry_verbs.principle: Keep the exact geometric vocabulary small, composable and semantically stable. Do not add a new canonical verb when a higher-level operation can be expressed as composition plus relations, parameters and policy.

doctrine.kernel_boundary: PLS-KERNEL-01 stores semantic identity/state/relations/history. It does not store OpenCascade TopoDS handles, Three.js object UUIDs, ACIS bodies, Parasolid tags or equivalent provider identity as canonical meaning.
doctrine.non_destructive_default: Geometry operations are non-destructive by default. Source entities, cutters, references and operation lineage remain addressable; the current B-Rep is an evaluated representation of accepted feature/transform history, not the sole durable design record.
doctrine.precision: Exactness is latent in ordinary interaction through snapping, numeric input, reference frames, constraints and tolerances rather than a separate ceremony-heavy modeling mode.
doctrine.provider_neutrality: Providers are replaceable executors of representation/geometry contracts. Adding or replacing a provider must not require migration of semantic world identity merely because implementation handles differ.
doctrine.resolver_not_kernel: The Plasma Geometry Resolver owns operation semantics, strategy selection, tolerance policy, semantic references, validation, healing and fallback. OpenCascade executes exact geometry algorithms beneath that resolver and may be patched, wrapped, supplemented or routed around without changing canonical meaning.
doctrine.same_path: Human gesture, language shortcut, agent plan, generator and imported edit resolve through the same typed OperationPlan → Transform path.
doctrine.surface: The user manipulates the designed world through a small verb set rather than provider-specific commands or a visible implementation graph.
doctrine.two_level_verb_model: Interaction verbs are optimized for humans and AI and may be contextual or compositional. Canonical geometry verbs are the stable semantic contract beneath them. Architectural commands such as Wall Junction, Opening, Beam End Cut or Roof Trim compile into canonical verbs plus persistent Relations/Transforms; they do not become kernel primitives.

fabrication_interoperability_contract.authority: An external system can be authoritative inside its explicitly bounded domain, but its result enters Plasma as Evidence and/or a proposed Transform; it does not silently overwrite the project world.
fabrication_interoperability_contract.learning_loop: Fabrication exceptions, actual process limits, RFIs, costs and as-built outcomes may update PLS-18/PLS-08 knowledge through governed evidence rather than being buried in one file.
fabrication_interoperability_contract.principle: Plasma should interoperate deeply with specialist fabrication CAD/CAM before assuming it must reproduce decades of tool-specific manufacturing depth.
fabrication_interoperability_contract.round_trip: Delegated outputs return with source system/version, input revision, exact file/model identity, assumptions, manufacturability/process findings, changed geometry/parameters and reconciliation status.

loops.flow: POINTER / TOUCH / PEN / VOICE / AI → INTERACTION VERB + SELECTION + MODIFIERS → CANONICAL GEOMETRY VERB(S) → PLS-GR-01 RESOLVER [CLASSIFY → INFER INTENT → CHOOSE STRATEGY → BIND SEMANTIC REFERENCES → APPLY TOLERANCE POLICY → EVALUATE → VALIDATE → HEAL → COMMIT] → PLS-KERNEL-01 WORLD TRANSACTION → DERIVED REPRESENTATIONS
loops.gap: The canonical verb and provider-neutral boundary are specified, and PLS-GR-01 now defines a staged resolver API, but implementation has not yet proven deterministic stage contracts, replayable decision evidence, bounded healing, semantic-reference rebinding and atomic commit across difficult geometric cases, repeated edits, provider regeneration and concurrent world revisions.

geometry_capability_contract.multi_provider_rule: One operation may use a fast interaction provider for preview and an exact provider for validation/commit; resulting representations remain tied to the same world revision and operation lineage.

provider_classes.exact_brep: Exact solid/surface/curve operations and tolerance-governed topology. Initial provider: OpenCascade; possible future providers include ACIS/Parasolid.
provider_classes.external_cad_cam: Specialist fabrication/detailing systems invoked through bounded interchange/connector contracts.
provider_classes.interactive_render: Low-latency display, picking, handles and proxy geometry. Initial provider: Three.js/WebGPU; not treated as an exact CAD kernel.
provider_classes.mesh_sdf_sculpt: Freeform, voxel/SDF, subdivision and sculptural realization where exact B-Rep is not the right interaction representation.

geometry_capability_contract.router_rule: Route by semantic need, required fidelity/tolerance, latency, topology identity, reproducibility, availability and policy—not by whichever provider happens to own the current viewport object.

commit_requires: topologically valid for the declared representation kind
manifold/closed where the contract requires a solid
history/provenance traceable and reversibly expressible as Plasma operations
free of unintended zero-area faces, micro-edges, sliver faces, duplicate same-domain topology or tolerance explosions beyond policy
deterministically reproducible from pinned inputs/provider/version/tolerance policy within declared reproducibility class
geometry_cleanliness_invariant.failure_behavior: Do not silently accept dirty geometry. Return a typed finding with the failing invariant, affected topology, measured tolerance/deviation, attempted strategies/healing and permitted user/agent resolutions.

acceptance_fixtures: TRIM prismatic beam to analytic wall face chooses analytic termination strategy and preserves beam semantic identity.
CONNECT two walls creates/maintains a junction Relation and may compose EXTEND/TRIM/SIMPLIFY without replacing the Relation with a fuse result.
SPLIT solid preserves all pieces and returns deterministic lineage/correspondence.
SUBTRACT hosted opening preserves cutter/host intent and does not make the cutter disappear from history.
Near-tangent and micro-gap cases either resolve within tolerance budget or return typed hold/failure without tolerance explosion.
Healing cannot exceed declared geometric deviation or change trim side/semantic postconditions.
A topology-changing edit that makes a hard face reference ambiguous blocks commit with TOPOLOGY_CORRESPONDENCE_AMBIGUOUS.
A stale base revision produces REVISION_CONFLICT and leaves accepted world unchanged.
Approximate preview followed by exact commit yields separately identified artifacts; preview geometry is never silently promoted.
Replaying identical pinned commit-candidate inputs reproduces the same strategy and result digest for deterministic strategy/provider classes.

determinism_and_concurrency.caching: Stage outputs may be cached only when all semantic inputs, policies, provider versions and dependency digests match. A viewport mesh cache may not satisfy an exact geometry cache key.
determinism_and_concurrency.concurrency: Optimistic. Evaluation may run concurrently, but commit compares against the pinned base revision and relevant causal slice before publication.
determinism_and_concurrency.idempotency: request_id + operation_id acts as an idempotency/correlation key for retries; duplicate successful commit requests must not create duplicate world mutations.

error_taxonomy.rule: Error codes are stable API semantics; provider-specific exceptions are nested diagnostics, not public control-flow identifiers.

optional_fields: candidate alternatives from upstream intent resolution
healing policy override within actor authority
rules: All quantities carry units; all geometry is interpreted in an explicit reference frame.
Targets are semantic Plasma references, never raw provider handles as canonical input.
A commit_candidate request pins the base world revision, policy versions, provider version and exactness requirements.
Hints may influence ranking but cannot weaken hard semantics, tolerance limits, invariants or authority.

geometry_resolver_api_contract.name: Plasma Geometry Resolver API

observability_and_evidence.explain: The UI/agent may ask why an operation failed or chose a strategy and receive the structured resolver trace rather than a reconstructed LLM narrative.
observability_and_evidence.privacy_and_size: Large B-Reps/meshes remain content-addressed artifacts; traces store stable references/digests and bounded diagnostics rather than duplicating geometry blobs.

provider_adapter_contract.isolation: A provider-specific crash, timeout or invalid result must not corrupt the resolver process or accepted world state.
provider_adapter_contract.open_cascade: Initial exact adapter. May expose BOPAlgo_Splitter, Boolean, intersection, sewing/healing and history signals internally, but these are implementation details beneath strategy IDs.
provider_adapter_contract.return_rule: Provider adapters return geometry artifacts and diagnostics; they do not commit Plasma state or decide semantic intent.

public_entrypoint.mutation_rule: Stages before commit operate on immutable inputs and isolated candidate artifacts. Only commit may propose a PLS-KERNEL-01 transaction against accepted world state.
public_entrypoint.preview_rule: Preview may end after evaluate/validate using an explicitly approximate representation. Preview artifacts are never accepted as exact commit artifacts unless they independently satisfy the exact contract and are revalidated for the commit request.
public_entrypoint.short_circuit_rule: Any stage may stop the pipeline with needs_input, held, unsupported, failed, stale or cancelled. No downstream stage may silently coerce an unresolved hard failure into success.

geometry_resolver_api_contract.purpose: Provide one deterministic, inspectable and provider-neutral contract for turning a canonical geometry verb into a validated candidate and, only when all geometric/semantic/world preconditions pass, an atomic Plasma world commit. The API owns resolution policy; geometry providers execute bounded strategies beneath it.

resolver_context.identity: Every context is keyed by request_id + base_world_revision + operation_id + policy/provider digests.
resolver_context.replay: Given identical pinned inputs and a deterministic provider class, the resolver must reproduce the same selected strategy, decisions and result digest or explicitly declare nondeterminism.

semantic_topology_finalize.position: Mandatory commit preflight after the final validate/heal result; implemented internally even though the public API keeps the nine major stages above.
semantic_topology_finalize.purpose: Rebuild old→new semantic sub-element correspondence after topology-changing evaluation/healing and expose confidence/ambiguity to commit.
semantic_topology_finalize.rule: Any hard downstream reference with ambiguous correspondence holds commit. Soft/advisory references may remain unresolved only if their consumers declare that this is acceptable.

stage_result_envelope.evidence_rule: A material resolver decision must be explainable from machine-readable stage evidence; free-text rationale alone is insufficient.

apply_tolerance_policy.growth_rule: Automatic tolerance widening is bounded and recorded. Exceeding the budget returns TOLERANCE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED; the resolver should try an equivalent strategy before requesting a policy change.
apply_tolerance_policy.responsibility: Translate Plasma tolerance policy into explicit bounded numerical parameters for this operation/provider.
apply_tolerance_policy.separation_rule: Kernel numerical tolerance, snap/acquisition tolerance, construction tolerance, fabrication tolerance, import reconciliation tolerance and display/picking tolerance remain distinct fields.

bind_semantic_references.responsibility: Resolve Plasma semantic references to the current provider subshapes/features needed by the selected strategy.
rules: Provider refs are scoped to this candidate evaluation and are not canonical world identity.
Hard dependent references require unambiguous binding before exact evaluation/commit.
If the referenced semantic role no longer exists, return UNBOUND_REFERENCE rather than choosing the nearest face by convenience.

choose_strategy.fallback_rule: Fallbacks must preserve the same canonical meaning and hard postconditions. A strategy may not change operation semantics merely to obtain a valid solid.
choose_strategy.ranking: Prefer analytic/reconstructive strategies over broad destructive Booleans when semantically equivalent; prefer strategies with stable topology correspondence and lower tolerance amplification.
choose_strategy.responsibility: Select the least-complex robust execution strategy/provider that satisfies the semantic postconditions.

examples: beam = prismatic solid with terminal-face role
wall = layered extrusion with structural exterior-face role
classify.responsibility: Normalize and classify the operation operands before any strategy is chosen.

commit.atomicity: Commit either advances the accepted world to one new immutable revision or changes nothing.
commit.identity_rule: Persist semantic operations, relations, parameters, provenance and correspondence—not raw provider handles as authoritative identity.
preconditions: base_world_revision is still current or concurrency policy explicitly permits branch commit
all hard semantic refs rebound unambiguously
topology correspondence rebuilt after any healing
commit.responsibility: Convert a fully resolved/validated candidate into one atomic PLS-KERNEL-01 world transaction.
commit.stale_rule: If the base revision changed incompatibly, return REVISION_CONFLICT/STALE_RESULT; never replay the old provider result onto the newer world without re-resolution.
commit.undo_rule: Undo/redo is represented as new inverse/replay Transforms/Events; history is not deleted.

evaluate.responsibility: Execute the selected strategy in an isolated candidate using the chosen geometry provider.
rules: No accepted world mutation occurs.
Provider crashes/failures are contained as typed results.
Commit-candidate exact evaluation pins provider/version and input digests.
Pointer-rate preview may use an approximate provider but must label fidelity/currentness explicitly.

forbidden_examples: move a design face materially to force closure
change which side of a trim is kept
increase tolerance beyond policy without explicit new decision
heal.responsibility: Apply only declared, bounded repairs that restore geometric cleanliness without changing design intent.
rules: Healing is optional; clean candidates pass through unchanged.
Every material repair is evidence-bearing and replayable.
Post-heal validation is mandatory.
If repair exceeds budget or changes semantic postconditions, return HEALING_EXCEEDS_POLICY/held.

infer_intent.responsibility: Resolve only bounded contextual meaning that is required to make the canonical verb executable.
rules: Explicit user/agent declarations outrank inferred defaults.
Only low-risk reversible defaults may be inferred silently.
Material ambiguity returns ambiguous/needs_input or explicit branch alternatives.
Intent resolution may refine how TRIM or CONNECT behaves but may not silently substitute a different canonical verb with materially different semantics.

validate.responsibility: Test both geometric integrity and the semantic effect requested by the operation.
validate.rule: A provider saying success is not sufficient. Validation is Plasma-owned and must verify the expected semantic result independently enough to detect plausible-but-wrong geometry.

geometry_resolver_contract.preview_commit_split: Pointer-rate preview may use GPU/proxy/mesh/SDF representations and bounded local checks. Pause/release/commit requests exact OpenCascade or equivalent geometry only for the affected causal/spatial region. The UI exposes currentness; approximate preview never silently becomes exact committed geometry.
geometry_resolver_contract.principle: Plasma resolves intent before invoking a geometry kernel. The resolver chooses the least-complex exact strategy that satisfies the declared semantic effect, tolerance and topology requirements.
geometry_resolver_contract.provider_fallback: If the selected exact strategy fails, retry/repair within bounded policy, choose an equivalent strategy/provider that satisfies the same semantic contract, or hold/branch/reject. Never silently change the operation meaning merely to obtain a valid solid.
stages: classify input geometry, semantic roles and existing relations
infer only bounded low-risk intent from context; preserve explicit ambiguity when material
choose exact strategy and provider based on operation semantics rather than current viewport representation
bind semantic references to current provider subshapes with confidence/ambiguity
apply Plasma tolerance policy and operation-specific limits
evaluate exact or approved approximate geometry in an isolated candidate
validate B-Rep/topology, manifold/closure/orientation and expected semantic effects
heal/simplify only within declared bounded policy; unify unintended same-domain micro-topology where safe
rebuild topology correspondence and detect lost/ambiguous references
commit atomically only after geometry, invariants and lineage requirements pass
geometry_resolver_contract.strategy_rule: Prefer direct analytic/reconstructive strategies over unnecessarily complex whole-solid Booleans when they produce the same semantic result more robustly. Example: trim a prismatic beam to a target plane by resolving the termination face rather than subtracting the entire wall solid when the wall is only a reference boundary.

junction_connection_contract.persistence_rule: The Relation remains canonical across regeneration. Exact faces/edges used to realize it may change and must be rebound through topology correspondence rather than treated as identity.
junction_connection_contract.principle: CONNECT/Junction establishes a persistent semantic relationship whose geometric realization may contain multiple canonical verbs; a junction is not synonymous with Boolean fuse.

loops.name: Spatial Operation + Kernel-Neutral Geometry Runtime
loops.next: Implement PLS-GR-01/0.1.0 as a reference Geometry Resolver service over OpenCascade for EXTEND, TRIM, SPLIT, CONNECT, SUBTRACT and FILLET. Each operation must execute through classify → inferIntent → chooseStrategy → bindSemanticReferences → applyTolerancePolicy → evaluate → validate → heal → commit, emitting stage evidence and deterministic error codes. Prove wall-wall junctions, beam-to-face trimming, hosted openings and split solids under exact, near-tangent, coincident, micro-gap, repeated-regeneration and stale-revision cases; exact commit must never reuse approximate preview geometry.

do_not: expose raw OpenCascade command semantics directly as the Plasma public API
treat TopoDS/subshape handles or numbering as canonical identity
allow provider-default tolerance growth to become implicit project policy
fork the entire kernel before failure classes are reproduced and isolated
extension_sequence: add specialist algorithm or bounded workaround for repeated failure class
contribute upstream or maintain a narrowly scoped patch where justified
route a declared operation class to another equivalent provider when needed
opencascade_hardening_policy.role: Initial exact B-Rep/NURBS execution provider under the Geometry Resolver.
use: operation history/persistent-naming signals as one input to Plasma topology correspondence

operation_plan_contract.ambiguity: A reversible preview may carry unresolved alternatives, but canonical commit must bind material referents, quantities, authority and preserve/break behavior or branch explicitly.
operation_plan_contract.no_direct_provider_edit: A provider-specific edit may calculate geometry, but the accepted effect must be expressible as Plasma Transform/State/Relation change plus derived representation lineage.
resolution_stages: compile to one or more typed Transform proposals

representation_failure_contract.commit_rule: No silent exact→approximate downgrade for commit-critical geometry. A verified alternate provider may satisfy the contract if it meets the same declared tolerance/identity/evidence requirements.
representation_failure_contract.display_rule: Display/analysis failure may degrade that view while leaving the world valid; the UI shows the failure/currentness rather than freezing or inventing geometry.
fallback_order: retry/repair within same semantic contract when bounded
alternate representation only if consumer contract permits

semantic_topology_reference_contract.failure_rule: If a materially referenced face/edge cannot be rebound unambiguously, the dependent exact result becomes failed/held rather than silently attaching to a different topology item.
semantic_topology_reference_contract.principle: Do not persist raw face/edge indexes as design references. Resolve semantic identity to current provider topology using multiple signals and record confidence.
resolution_order: semantic feature/role reference, e.g. wall.structural_exterior_face or beam.terminal_face

loops.summary: Compile simple human/AI interaction verbs into a stable canonical geometry language, then resolve those verbs through provider-neutral execution plans. The canonical layer defines geometric meaning—such as EXTEND, TRIM, SPLIT, CONNECT, SUBTRACT and OFFSET—while the Geometry Resolver chooses robust algorithms, tolerances, references, validation/healing and fallback. OpenCascade is the initial exact B-Rep/NURBS executor and Three.js/WebGPU the initial interactive representation provider; neither owns Plasma identity or intent.

tolerance_policy.principle: Tolerance belongs to Plasma policy, not ad-hoc provider defaults. Values are project/representation/operation scoped and recorded with lineage; exact numeric defaults must be validated empirically for project scale and provider behaviour.
rules: Do not conflate user snap distance with B-Rep coincidence tolerance.
Fuzzy Boolean tolerances, healing limits and import reconciliation must be explicit and bounded.
Tolerance growth across repeated operations is measured and may block commit when it exceeds policy.
Healing may not alter design intent merely to make invalid geometry pass.

topology_identity_contract.failure: Topology identity loss is a first-class representation failure. Commit is held when downstream hard relations depend on unresolved correspondence.
topology_identity_contract.principle: Provider topology is unstable implementation detail; Plasma requires semantic/persistent correspondence above it.
topology_identity_contract.result: Return correspondence with confidence/ambiguity rather than silently rebinding a materially changed face/edge to an old semantic identity.

acceptance_tests: Accept Regulation v2 that supersedes v1; Project A pinned to v1 remains unchanged and reproducible.
Impact analysis identifies exactly which projects/decisions depend on v1 and distinguishes grandfathered/unaffected cases.
Migrate Project B from v1→v2 only through an isolated branch and explicit approval; Project A stays on v1.
A later manufacturer capability update can be adopted for one fabrication package without forcing a regulatory baseline change.
Reproduce an old compliance decision with the exact KnowledgeUseTrace, source versions, assumptions and project revision.
Present two conflicting interpretations of an ambiguous clause without silently collapsing them into one rule.
An AI answer using stale latent knowledge cannot outrank a newer governed ledger source without explicit contrary evidence.

feedback: adjust confidence/applicability or propose new KnowledgeItem
calibration_contract.principle: Prediction-versus-outcome is evidence about knowledge quality, not automatic proof of a new universal rule.
calibration_contract.relationship_to_pls08: PLS-08 retrieves and learns context-bounded practice evidence; PLS-18 supplies durable version/supersession/baseline semantics so practice memory cannot silently generalize or rewrite projects.

doctrine.immutability: Accepted KnowledgeItem versions are immutable. Corrections and supersession create new versions/links; they do not overwrite historical content.
doctrine.model_independence: AI model weights are not the authoritative knowledge store. Agents retrieve exact ledger items and evidence, state unknowns, and leave a KnowledgeUseTrace for consequential reasoning.
doctrine.non_migration: Accepting knowledge into the ledger is not permission to mutate projects. Project adoption/migration is a separate governed decision/Transform.
doctrine.separation: World = what Plasma believes about this project at a revision. Knowledge Ledger = versioned propositions/rules/capabilities believed generally or contextually outside a single project.
doctrine.temporal_truth: Old knowledge may remain the correct governing baseline for a project because of permit date, contract, grandfathering, procurement state or explicit authority. “Latest” and “applicable” are not synonyms.

loops.flow: AUTHORITATIVE / PRACTICE / VENDOR SOURCE → SOURCE WATCHER / INGEST → CANDIDATE KNOWLEDGE VERSION → PARSE + PROVENANCE + APPLICABILITY + CONFLICT CHECK → HUMAN/GOVERNED ACCEPTANCE INTO APPEND-ONLY LEDGER → IMPACT ANALYSIS AGAINST PROJECT BASELINES → NOTIFY / REVIEW / BRANCH MIGRATION IF CHOSEN → PROJECT DECISION REFERENCES EXACT KNOWLEDGE VERSION(S) → OUTCOME/EVIDENCE FEEDS CALIBRATION
loops.gap: PLS-07 and PLS-08 model project epistemics and contextual practice evidence, but the consolidated spec does not yet define a durable general knowledge ledger, immutable supersession chain, source watchers, project-stage baseline pins, knowledge-use traces or migration rules. Without them, approving a newer regulation/vendor standard could accidentally rewrite legacy project reasoning or make old decisions impossible to reproduce.

impact_and_migration_contract.impact: For an accepted new version, identify projects/baselines/decisions/entities/evaluations that referenced the superseded item or whose applicability envelope intersects the change.
impact_and_migration_contract.legacy_rule: Closed, permitted, contracted, fabricated or archived projects may intentionally remain on historical baselines indefinitely, subject to explicit legal/safety override processes outside ordinary update flow.
impact_and_migration_contract.migration_flow: candidate baseline → isolated branch → recompute affected rules/representations/cost/fabrication consequences → compare → named authority decision → governed Transform/commit or retain prior baseline
impact_and_migration_contract.no_auto_override: Impact analysis produces work/notifications, never bulk mutation merely because an administrator approved a source update.

knowledge_item_contract.authority_rule: Source authority, interpretation confidence and project applicability are separate dimensions.

knowledge_use_trace_contract.ai_rule: AI may summarize and reason over knowledge but must not cite its own latent memory as equivalent to an authoritative source where a governed source is required.
knowledge_use_trace_contract.reproducibility: A consequential historical decision should be explainable using the exact source/knowledge versions and project state that existed when it was made.

loops.name: Knowledge Ledger + Project Baseline Governance
loops.next: Build one Victorian regulation + fabrication knowledge vertical slice. Ingest two superseding rule versions and two manufacturer capability versions; pin Project A to the older applicable baseline and Project B to the newer one; run update impact analysis; prove that accepting new knowledge changes neither project automatically; migrate only Project B on an isolated branch; reproduce an old decision from its original knowledge-use trace.

project_baseline_contract.branching: Proposed baseline migration is rehearsed on a branch, with affected decisions/entities/evaluations enumerated before promotion.
project_baseline_contract.granularity: A project may keep an older regulatory baseline while adopting newer manufacturer/fabrication knowledge where allowed; exceptions are explicit and auditable.
project_baseline_contract.rule: A project decision resolves knowledge through its active baseline plus explicit exceptions, not through a global “latest” pointer.

source_update_contract.ambiguity: Ambiguous or conflicting updates remain contested/unknown with linked interpretations; an approval may accept one interpretation for a defined scope without deleting alternatives.
candidate_flow: capture immutable source snapshot/digest where lawful
source_update_contract.staleness: Knowledge items and source watchers carry currentness. Unchecked freshness may reduce confidence or trigger review but does not retroactively rewrite historical decisions.
source_update_contract.watcher: Configured source families may be checked on schedules or by external notifications. New content enters as candidate knowledge, not active truth.

loops.summary: Separate general, versioned knowledge from project world truth. Standards, regulations, manufacturer data, fabrication capability, internal practice and learned outcomes live in an append-only Knowledge Ledger with authority, jurisdiction, applicability and temporal validity. Projects pin explicit knowledge baselines; source updates trigger candidate ingestion and impact analysis, never silent migration of older or grandfathered work.

meta.architecture_posture: one Plasma environment over coupled project and capability states; a minimal semantic Plasma Kernel owns Entity, State, Relation, Transform, Invariant, Event and Evidence plus governed transaction semantics; all canonical mutation is transform-only against immutable revisions; human, touch, voice and AI interaction resolve through a small spatial-verb/operation layer into typed Transforms before entering the kernel; semantic state compiles into replaceable graph/matrix/tensor/geometry/solver representations without surrendering authority; geometry providers and render/interaction engines are kernel-neutral capability adapters rather than owners of identity; representation requests/responses carry explicit fidelity, tolerance, currentness, provenance and failure semantics; project truth is separated from a versioned general Knowledge Ledger, and accepted decisions pin exact knowledge baselines so later source updates trigger impact analysis rather than silent project migration; specialist fabrication/CAD/CAM systems may remain authoritative for bounded manufacturing operations while Plasma retains design intent, cross-domain state, provenance and reconciliation; graph structures are revision-pinned projections rather than alternate truth stores; bounded reactive execution is extended by durable work orchestration; pathology/anti-pattern evaluation screens proposals without converting convention into law; protected lifeboat controls remain non-self-modifiable; immutable release bundles; AI and external ecosystems are replaceable actors/capability providers; ADK remains non-prerequisite development machinery; Spectrum research remains non-blocking; canonical geometry verbs are stable semantic operations above provider algorithms; a Plasma Geometry Resolver classifies intent, selects exact strategy, applies tolerance/reference policy, validates/heals results and commits only clean attributable geometry; junctions remain semantic relationships with geometric resolution, not raw Booleans
meta.document_lineage: Continues v0.4.24. Strengthens PLS-17 with a canonical geometry-verb vocabulary and a governed Geometry Resolver over OpenCascade. Separates user-facing interaction verbs from stable geometric semantics; formalizes EXTEND/TRIM/SPLIT/MERGE, CONNECT/DISCONNECT/ALIGN/PROJECT, IMPRINT/SECTION, UNION/SUBTRACT/INTERSECT, OFFSET/THICKEN/SHELL/SWEEP/LOFT, FILLET/CHAMFER and SEW/HEAL/SIMPLIFY; defines junctions as persistent relationships rather than raw Booleans; centralizes tolerance policy; requires semantic topology references above provider IDs; adds classify→infer→strategy→evaluate→validate→clean→commit resolver stages; codifies fast-preview/exact-commit separation, clean-geometry invariants, OCCT hardening/fallback rules and regression-corpus expectations. OpenCascade remains the initial exact geometry executor, not the source of world truth. The seven kernel primitives and transaction lifecycle remain unchanged.
meta.name: Plasma / Foundry
meta.reproducibility_status: not-yet-proven; canonical repository extraction and release-bundle evidence required

plasma_kernel.acceptance: The seven primitives and transaction semantics are accepted only if the unchanged kernel can represent and govern wall movement, terrain editing, rule change, window replacement, area recalculation, simulation, branching, AI proposal acceptance, human decision, stale drawing invalidation, external robot action and as-built observation through domain schemas/capability adapters rather than new kernel primitives.

canonicality.authoritative: typed semantic world state plus immutable revision/event/evidence lineage
canonicality.derived: representations, analyses, compiled graphs/matrices/tensors, meshes, B-Reps, USD, solver models and caches
canonicality.external: survey, regulation, weather, manufacturer, consultant and other evidence-bearing sources
canonicality.rule: Derived or external representations never become canonical Plasma truth by implication. Promotion requires a governed Transform/Transaction.

capability_boundary.geometry_provider_rule: Geometry and display providers implement declared capability contracts behind neutral requests. OpenCascade is the initial exact B-Rep/NURBS provider and Three.js is an initial interactive/render representation provider; neither leaks implementation identity into canonical world state. ACIS, Parasolid, mesh/SDF/sculptural engines or future providers may be added or routed per operation without rewriting the world model.
capability_boundary.principle: Plasma owns architectural/domain meaning and governed state transition; external ecosystems provide replaceable specialized computation.
capability_boundary.specialist_fabrication_rule: Plasma does not require replacement of Fusion, Inventor, SolidWorks, CAM or machine software. It may delegate bounded fabrication operations to specialist systems under an explicit ownership map, then ingest geometry, manufacturability, process limits, cost, machine outcomes and exceptions as Evidence and/or proposed Transforms. External task success never self-promotes to project truth.
capability_boundary.vendor_rule: No external engine, scene graph, AI model, CAD kernel, solver or vendor API is canonical owner of the Plasma world.

compilation.authority_rule: Compiled forms are reproducible derived artefacts keyed to exact input revisions and producer versions.
compilation.principle: Matrices/tensors are machine representations of transformations and dependencies, not the human/domain ontology.

dependency_model.runtime_rule: Semantic dependencies remain authoritative; runtimes may compile them to adjacency lists, sparse matrices, execution DAGs or GPU-friendly structures for localized propagation.

purposes: detect emergent geometry/topology/system conditions not knowable from operations alone
run domain anti-pattern, compliance, fabrication, construction, cost and coherence evaluators
evaluate cross-entity, cross-system and solver-derived consequences
candidate_world.rule: Findings are revision-pinned evaluation artefacts with evidence/currentness; they do not mutate canonical state and do not become Invariants merely by being detected.
candidate_world.timing: During DERIVE/EVALUATE after the isolated candidate world exists.

purposes: detect temporal anti-patterns such as type proliferation or repeated rework
detect system/project pathologies that no single transaction reveals
propose new project/organization anti-pattern definitions from accumulated evidence
history_and_project.rule: Learned definitions remain proposed until validated and promoted through governed evidence/authority; recurrence is evidence, not automatic truth.
history_and_project.timing: Outside the pointer hot path, incrementally over committed events, revisions, assemblies, project metrics and organization evidence.

purposes: reject structurally corrupt primitive operations before they contaminate a candidate world
surface known high-confidence anti-patterns at the inception of a proposed change
select additional evaluators required by the affected closure
estimate whether deeper candidate-world evaluation is required
preflight.rule: Preflight may short-circuit a transaction only when the returned finding carries blocking authority under kernel integrity, an active hard Invariant, or an explicitly authorized domain policy. Advisory novelty/plausibility findings cannot block by themselves.
preflight.timing: After DECLARE/EXPAND and once IMPACT has identified the smallest determinable affected closure, before expensive APPLY/DERIVE work where the issue can be inferred from proposed primitive operations, schemas, topology, authority or known local conditions.

evaluation_hooks.principle: The kernel exposes governed evaluator hooks around the existing transaction lifecycle without defining domain-specific evaluator ontologies. Anti-pattern/pathology detection is one consumer of these hooks, not an eighth primitive.
evaluation_hooks.result_contract: Evaluator results may be stored as Evidence-linked evaluation artefacts and transaction diagnostics; authoritative world change still occurs only through Transform/Transaction semantics.

kernel_invariants: K4 canonical mutation through transactions only
K9 domain evaluators and anti-pattern findings cannot directly mutate canonical state or silently promote themselves to Invariants
K10 provider neutrality: canonical semantic identity may not depend on OpenCascade, Three.js, ACIS, Parasolid, IFC, USD or other provider-specific object/topology handles
K11 representation honesty: derived representation currentness, approximation and failure remain explicit; provider failure cannot silently falsify, validate or mutate authoritative world state

K12 knowledge temporal integrity: acceptance of a newer general knowledge/source version never silently rewrites an accepted project world; project decisions and migrations reference explicit immutable knowledge/evidence versions

persistence.atomicity_rule: The browser reference store publishes one complete versioned envelope through a single synchronous key replacement; future database implementations may differ physically but must preserve all-or-nothing accepted revision publication and validation before promotion.
persistence.failure_rule: Invalid primary bytes never silently become canonical state. Backup/legacy recovery must expose source and diagnostics.
persistence.reopen_rule: A fresh runtime must reconstruct the accepted branch head, immutable states, Event/Transform lineage and application-aligned accepted state from persisted bytes without relying on the previous in-memory kernel object.

Entity.definition: Anything requiring persistent identity through state change.

Event.definition: Immutable historical record of what actually occurred, distinct from the Transform that proposed change.

Evidence.definition: First-class provenance explaining why Plasma believes a state, relation, invariant, evaluation, transform or event.

Invariant.definition: Typed proposition, condition, target or preference evaluated against a candidate or accepted world.

Relation.definition: Typed directed or symmetric connection between entities.
Relation.rule: Domain relation vocabularies are schema-defined above the kernel; the kernel preserves typed identity and integrity.

State.definition: Typed values asserted about an Entity at a specific immutable world revision.
State.unit_rule: Physical quantities carry explicit units; large payloads are referenced rather than embedded.

Transform.definition: Typed proposed operation mapping one world state to a candidate world state.
Transform.rule: Higher-level operations compile to primitive operations; direct mutation of accepted canonical state is forbidden.

plasma_kernel.purpose: Smallest persistent computational substrate required to represent and evolve a designed world without encoding architecture-specific object classes in the kernel.

Environment policy blocks navigable localhost/file origins, so normal-origin OS/browser durability remains unobserved; production database stores, exact geometry, shared-store concurrency, workers and physical-device latency remain unproven.
reference_slice.promotion_rule: Later domain implementations may claim kernel conformance only if their domain actions reduce to the unchanged seven primitives and pass equivalent transaction, lineage, conflict, concurrency and branch semantics.
reference_slice.test_status: reference semantics 5/5 Node pass; live browser conflict/accept/undo pass; persistent R1 reconstructs in a fresh browser JS realm; undo-after-reopen R2 passes; corrupted primary checksum falls back to valid R1 backup; desktop/mobile pointer regression suite passes with no runtime exceptions

plasma_kernel.thesis: W[t+1] = Commit(Evaluate(T(W[t]))) subject to active invariants and authority.

transaction.atomicity: Canonical commit is all-or-nothing for the authorised transaction boundary.
transaction.concurrency: Optimistic concurrency: every transaction names a base revision; stale-base transactions rebase only when touched resources are provably independent, otherwise conflict or branch.

entry_contract.ambiguity_rule: Material ambiguity may remain during reversible preview but must be resolved, explicitly branched or presented for authority before canonical commit.
entry_contract.boundary: PLS-KERNEL-01 begins with typed Transform(s), not raw pointer, voice, natural-language or vendor-kernel commands.
entry_contract.provider_rule: A provider-specific command or object handle is never a canonical Transform by itself; it is an execution detail of a typed operation.
entry_contract.upstream_resolution: PLS-14/PLS-17 resolve actor intent, selection, spatial verb, numeric parameters, modifiers, ambiguity, authority and required representations into one or more typed Transform proposals.

transaction.preview: Interactive preview is an isolated speculative candidate world, not accepted canonical state. PLS-16 findings may annotate the preview but must respect the PLS-10 latency budget; expensive/project-scale scans run on release or in background work.

representation_failure_policy.commit_critical: If an exact representation or evaluator is declared required to establish a hard invariant, topology identity, manufacturing condition or operation result, canonical commit is held until that requirement succeeds or an explicitly equivalent verified provider/fallback satisfies the same contract.
representation_failure_policy.no_silent_downgrade: The runtime may not replace an exact requested contract with an approximate result without making the fallback and achieved tolerance explicit.
representation_failure_policy.noncritical: If the failed representation is display-, analysis- or refinement-only and not required for commit, the world may remain valid while that representation is marked failed/stale/unavailable/unknown.
representation_failure_policy.preview: Speculative interaction may continue on a proxy/approximate representation when policy allows, but the UI must disclose degraded fidelity/currentness and may not imply exact validation.
representation_failure_policy.principle: A failed derived representation is not automatically a failed or invalid world. Failure is explicit state with scope, revision and producer provenance.
representation_failure_policy.stale_result: Any response pinned to a superseded world/input revision is rejected or retained only as historical evidence; it cannot silently overwrite a newer representation.

semantics.APPLY: Execute operations against an isolated candidate world.
semantics.BEGIN: Pin immutable base revision and authority context.
semantics.COMMIT: Atomically publish all authorised canonical operations as a new immutable revision or publish none.
semantics.DECLARE: Receive one or more typed high-level Transforms and rationale.
semantics.DERIVE: Mark affected derived state current/stale/computing/failed/unknown and recompute only what policy/fidelity requires.
semantics.EMIT: Append Events, evidence links, invalidations, representation updates and subscriptions/messages.
semantics.EVALUATE: Evaluate active Invariants and required revision-pinned evaluators intersecting the affected closure, including candidate-world pathology/anti-pattern checks where applicable, with explicit evidence/currentness and blocking authority.
semantics.EXPAND: Compile high-level Transforms into primitive kernel operations without mutating accepted state.
semantics.IMPACT: Compute the smallest determinable semantic/spatial dependency closure and required evaluators. Invoke eligible preflight checks as soon as enough scope is known; structurally corrupt operations or explicitly blocking governed findings may stop before candidate application.
semantics.RESOLVE: Classify invariant and evaluator outcomes as pass, advisory, review, soft conflict, hard conflict, corrupting, or unknown; optionally return typed alternative Transform proposals, remediation and governed exception paths.

transaction.undo: Undo is a new inverse or compensating Transform/Event; committed history is never erased.

world_revision.branch_rule: Branches share immutable ancestry and diverge through event streams; a branch is not a duplicated project by definition.

policy.adk_role: Bounded development machinery presented within the unified Plasma environment; it may invoke Plasma contracts but is not a prerequisite for Plasma Runtime.
policy.ai_reasoning_posture_rule: Plasma does not attempt to hard-code general intelligence. AI is a replaceable actor that selects and composes typed reasoning operators, calls deterministic tools and proposes state transitions; Plasma owns world identity, evidence, constraints, dependency/currentness, validation, commitments, authority and immutable revision lineage.
policy.as_designed_as_built_rule: Accepted design state and observed physical state are maintained separately and compared explicitly; deviation does not mutate either history by implication.
policy.bidirectional_trace_rule: Every authoritative project result must be traceable to the exact capability and version that produced it; every candidate capability change must expose the project entities, derivations and coherent worlds it may affect.
policy.bounded_reactivity_rule: A world-state mutation invalidates the smallest determinable semantic and spatial dependency closure. Plasma restores local invariants synchronously within an interaction budget, propagates only across materially changed boundary conditions, and restores regional/global invariants asynchronously.
policy.coherent_promotion_rule: Promotion is an explicit human-authorised transaction that advances both the accepted capability version and a coherent project revision; failed or rejected candidates remain inspectable without contaminating the active world.
policy.compatibility_rule: Every dependency declares an accepted version range and exact active pin. Incompatible changes require an explicit migration or parallel reader plus affected-world analysis.
policy.constraint_crossing_rule: Direct manipulation may cross a hard constraint inside a clearly speculative/conflicted preview so design intent is not silently clamped or erased. The exact limiting boundary remains visible. Promotion to a coherent authoritative revision is blocked until the hard conflict is resolved or the governing rule is changed through a separately authorized decision.
policy.context_capsule_rule: AI/tool work receives the smallest revision-pinned context capsule needed for the declared task: active semantic/dependency slice, invariants/rules, evidence/currentness, required representations, tools/versions, authority and output contract. Model context is disposable execution input, not project memory or authority.
policy.context_readiness_rule: Feasibility may be explored on incomplete context, but Plasma must visibly distinguish exploratory from decision-grade feasibility. Decision-grade status requires declared critical-context coverage or explicit accepted assumptions/waivers for unresolved items.
policy.contextual_development_rule: A project discrepancy may create a development task carrying the selected world objects, revision IDs, producer versions, assumptions, failed evidence and expected outcome as bounded context.
policy.coupled_state_rule: Project state and capability/development state remain distinct typed state spaces joined by explicit identity, provenance, dependency, affected-world and evidence edges.
policy.cycle_resolution_rule: Relevant dependency/execution projections must detect cycles/strongly connected components before DAG scheduling. Cycles become explicit bounded solve units with declared method, convergence/stop criteria, iteration/resource limit and failure policy; non-convergence never silently publishes the last iterate as valid.
policy.dependency_latency_rule: Dependencies declare propagation semantics such as direct, local-hard, local-soft, regional, global or advisory so runtime urgency is distinct from semantic importance.
policy.dependency_not_causality_rule: A derivation, invalidation or execution dependency does not by itself establish physical or logical causation. Causal assertions are typed claims requiring method/evidence; dependency edges remain operational unless explicitly promoted as a causal claim.
policy.dirty_region_rule: Changes produce explicit invalidation envelopes and dirty sets. Dependency propagation stops when affected boundary summaries remain unchanged and expands only when a changed result can materially affect another region.
policy.durable_work_rule: Long-running ExecutionPlans and WorkItems persist enough identity, input revisions, producer versions, attempt/idempotency state, outputs/evidence and diagnostics to validate and resume after restart. Stale or incompatible work is superseded rather than silently reused.
policy.dynamic_dependency_rule: Derived spatial, topological, rule-applicability, solver and interaction dependencies are revisioned and may appear/disappear as world state changes. Dependency discovery has explicit freshness/completeness state; absent edges cannot be treated as proof of no consequence when discovery is incomplete.
policy.edit_scaling_rule: The cost of an ordinary edit should scale primarily with the affected semantic/spatial region and requested fidelity, not with total project size. Benchmarking must report active-set size, dirty-set size, propagation depth, materialised representation fidelity, immediate coherence latency and full convergence latency.
policy.evidence_applicability_rule: Evidence is context-specific and must not be generalized by default. Every reusable claim or case carries an applicability envelope including jurisdiction/authority, governing-version/time, site and regulatory context, project/building type and scale, material physical conditions, proposal characteristics, decision stage/pathway and known decision-maker context. Historical evidence may support a current decision only after an explicit context-match assessment.
policy.evidence_immutability_rule: Machine evidence is append-only and content-addressed; corrections supersede but do not erase previous evidence.
policy.evidence_non_promotion_rule: Project outcomes, consultant opinions, authority comments and practice patterns never silently become governing rules or statutory truth. Plasma preserves a hierarchy of governing rule → authoritative interpretation → project outcome → practice pattern → heuristic → current-project inference, with explicit promotion prohibited across these classes without governed evidence and review.
policy.evidence_packet_rule: Evidence is stored and retrieved as sparse object-centred packets attached to sites, context entities, rules, design objects, issues and decisions. The runtime may use a large graph internally, but user-facing retrieval is decision-scoped and similarity-ranked rather than table-scoped.
policy.evidence_ui_rule: Humans manage exceptions and decisions, not evidence records. Evidence is surfaced through the project object, question, decision, dependency or risk that makes it relevant, using progressive disclosure Result → Why → Evidence → Sources/History. Direct database or spreadsheet browsing is an expert/debug view, never the primary workflow.
policy.external_side_effect_rule: Pure computation, reversible local work, compensatable external writes and irreversible/high-consequence actions are distinct WorkItem classes. Scheduling permission never implies side-effect authority; robotics/fabrication/submission/purchase-class actions require explicit preflight authority and post-action evidence.
policy.fabrication_realization_rule: A sculptural design realization is not automatically construction-valid. Plasma derives and validates a separate fabrication realization with declared process constraints such as watertightness, minimum thickness, curvature/radius, draft, tooling, support, material behaviour and connection geometry as applicable.
policy.field_compression_rule: Where semantics permit, dense many-to-many physical relationships should be represented by shared spatial fields or hierarchical summaries instead of explicit pairwise graph edges, reducing dependency cardinality while preserving inspectable causality.
policy.frame_edit_rule: Every human/AI geometric command names its coordinate frame and units. The initial site and building frames remain distinct until an explicit placement transform is accepted. No implicit coordinate conversion.
policy.graph_projection_rule: Plasma has one authoritative semantic world. Semantic/relation, dependency/invalidation, evidence/provenance and execution/work graphs are revision-pinned projections or compiled structures, never independent mutation authorities or alternate truth stores.
policy.hierarchical_summary_rule: Cross-region and global checks should consume stable semantic summaries at the highest meaningful level before descending into detailed children. Global stability should be enforced through a compact set of invariants rather than universal graph traversal.
policy.human_ai_edit_rule: Humans and AI use the same typed domain operations and proposal validation. AI commands include stable request identity, accepted revision and expected proposal revision; active gestures and stale bases reject competing proposals. Duplicate retries never reapply additive grading. Human review controls acceptance.
policy.independent_evaluation_rule: A candidate capability may not be proven solely by the agent, prompt, evaluator or test suite that it modified. Promotion requires evidence from an unchanged or independently governed evaluation path.
policy.interaction_budget_rule: Runtime scheduling protects direct manipulation with explicit latency budgets: pointer/viewport feedback first, local constraint validity next, rich preview/refinement after interaction, and regional/global validation asynchronously unless a hard commit invariant requires blocking.
policy.interaction_kernel_boundary_rule: High-frequency pointer/viewport feedback may use bounded speculative local state for latency, but release/accept must cross the canonical PLS-KERNEL-01 transaction boundary before accepted state changes. UI preview state is never canonical by implication.
policy.invariant_taxonomy_rule: Invariant is the general kernel contract for hard requirements, soft constraints, optimisation targets, preferences and advisories. Evaluations return pass, fail, unknown, stale or not-applicable with values, margins, confidence, evidence and evaluator identity where applicable.
policy.kernel_extraction_rule: Do not introduce a new Spectrum kernel primitive until multiple independent Plasma cases expose the same irreducible gap in established methods.
policy.kernel_primitive_rule: The canonical Plasma semantic kernel is limited to Entity, State, Relation, Transform, Invariant, Event and Evidence. Domain concepts such as wall, room, terrain, structure, planning rule, drawing, robot and simulation are schemas/compositions above the kernel unless repeated independent failures demonstrate a missing universal primitive.
policy.kernel_recovery_rule: Corrupt or incompatible persisted state may not be silently accepted. Validate before promotion; recover only from an explicit valid backup/migration path and expose the recovery source and diagnostics.
policy.legacy_world_state_mapping_rule: Earlier PLS-01 structures such as ChangeSet, OperationRecord, DerivedResult, DerivationRecord and CoherentCut remain valid runtime/index/projection structures where useful, but they are not additional Plasma Kernel primitives; they must map onto or derive from Entity, State, Relation, Transform, Invariant, Event and Evidence plus immutable revisions/transactions.
policy.model_independent_gesture_rule: Per-pointer-update interaction must not depend on an LLM/model response. Deterministic geometry, locality, currentness and commit-critical local validation protect direct manipulation; AI may assist after conflict, release, idle or explicit request through the same typed proposal/reasoning contracts.
policy.morphology_ownership_rule: Plasma owns stable identity, intent, morphology, semantic regions, attachments, constraints and accepted realizations even when a surface is generated by AI or edited in an external sculpting application. External tools are authoring adapters, not alternate sources of truth.
policy.multiresolution_sculpt_rule: Sculptural edits operate at explicit levels such as topology/skeleton, major masses, secondary form, surface features and microdetail. Upstream edits may deform or reproject downstream detail; microdetail edits must not unnecessarily invalidate architectural dependencies.
policy.observation_authority_rule: Sensor-derived and reconstructed data remains observed evidence; inferred semantics, identity and correspondence remain claims until promoted through typed validate/commit.
policy.observation_backend_rule: Real-to-sim implementations are replaceable adapters. Lucida-style systems may provide parse/generate/place reconstruction, but Plasma owns observation artifacts, provenance, correspondence, uncertainty, currentness and promotion contracts.
policy.parallel_compute_rule: Plasma is explicitly multicore-CPU and GPU aware. Irregular graph traversal, event scheduling, sparse constraints, topology and exact-geometry orchestration favour CPU workers; dense homogeneous spatial/field/candidate evaluations favour GPU compute. Parallelism is scheduled by dependency, locality, cost and latency rather than enabled indiscriminately.
policy.performance_boundaries_rule: Every interactive or background computation is governed explicitly by five boundaries: Active World (what is computationally relevant now), Dirty Frontier (what actually changed), Dependency Horizon (how far consequences must propagate now), Representation LOD (what fidelity the operation requires), and Consistency Horizon (what must be correct immediately versus what may converge asynchronously). These boundaries are runtime contracts and observability dimensions, not optional optimisations.
policy.persistent_kernel_rule: Accepted kernel state must be recoverable from a validated versioned store independent of the prior process memory. Persistence format is replaceable; identity, revision ancestry, Transform/Event/Evidence lineage, atomic commit and failure visibility are not.
policy.perspective_economy_rule: Do not instantiate a separate autonomous agent merely to represent every viewpoint. Prefer lightweight reasoning lenses composed by one capable actor unless genuine concurrency, independent authority, tool isolation or adversarial independence justifies separate agents.
policy.practice_learning_rule: Feasibility outputs are hypotheses, not self-training truth. Practice learning occurs by later reconciling a recorded prediction and its assumptions against live-project authority interactions and outcomes. Divergence is retained as evidence rather than overwritten, enabling institutional learning without circular reinforcement.
policy.preview_commit_rule: Interactive preview state is a bounded speculative branch distinct from the last coherent authoritative world. Commit promotes only validated mutations and never implies that deferred regional/global derived state is already current.
policy.progressive_correctness_rule: Global correctness is governed by eventual validated convergence, not by recomputing the entire world during each local interaction. Derived state explicitly reports current, stale, updating, pending or conflicted status against its input revisions.
policy.protected_kernel_rule: The protected lifeboat is the non-self-modifiable operational subset around the Plasma Kernel: versioning, permissions/authority, event/evidence identity, rollback, approval and recovery. Candidate capability changes cannot rewrite these controls during their own evaluation.
policy.reality_evidence_rule: Plasma must not silently treat imported, reconstructed or inferred context as reality. Physical/legal/regulatory/economic facts enter as evidence-bearing claims with source, capture/acquisition time, coordinate reference, authority, uncertainty, currency and provenance before promotion to accepted context.
policy.reasoning_composition_rule: Reusable intelligence should be expressed as small operator compositions selected for the current question rather than as a growing catalogue of bespoke prompt workflows. Add or specialize an operator only after multiple materially different cases expose a recurring need that existing operators cannot express cleanly.
policy.reasoning_lens_rule: A Reasoning Lens is a declared context for interrogating the same authoritative world object from a role, discipline, stakeholder, jurisdiction, purpose, fidelity or risk posture. It may change questions, criteria and weighting but must not duplicate the object, silently create competing facts or mutate accepted state.
policy.reasoning_operator_rule: Plasma separates epistemic state from reasoning operation. Observe, interpret, infer, question, propose, challenge, compare, evaluate, perspective, test, decide and revise are typed composable operations over evidence, claims, intent and world state; they do not constitute an alternate source of truth.
policy.reasoning_trace_rule: Plasma records public reasoning artefacts and transitions—operator/version, question, lens, cited inputs, tools/rules/solvers, output claim/proposal/evaluation, uncertainty/status, actor and causal/supersession links—so decisions are explainable and replayable. Private model chain-of-thought is neither required nor authoritative provenance.
policy.reasoning_validation_rule: The initial reasoning-operator abstraction is accepted only if one small vocabulary works across terrain/driveway, coupled bedroom movement and planning interpretation without domain-specific semantic distortion. Failed mappings are evidence to change the abstraction before broad implementation.
policy.reference_slice_rule: PLS-KERNEL-01-WALL-REF-01 is the executable semantic acceptance slice for kernel conformance: +500 mm must conflict without accepted mutation, +150 mm must commit atomically, stale-base commit must conflict, branches must remain isolated, and undo must append rather than erase history.
policy.release_rule: Only a complete immutable Plasma release bundle may be promoted. Latest individual components are never assembled implicitly in an active environment.
policy.representation_edit_rule: Interaction must distinguish edits to authoritative geometry/intent from representation-only edits; changing a generated stair break mark must not silently change stair geometry.
policy.representation_lod_rule: Semantic LOD, geometric LOD and graphic representation are related but remain distinct dimensions.
policy.representation_separation_rule: Authoritative semantic objects, physical geometry and view representations are distinct state. No architectural element owns a single canonical drawing representation.
policy.representation_trace_rule: Generated graphic primitives retain traceability to the object, View Contract and grammar rule that produced them so Plasma can explain why each line, symbol, break, arrow or annotation exists.
policy.revision_cancellation_rule: Every asynchronous computation carries world/input revisions and producer versions. Superseded work is cancelled where possible or discarded on completion; stale results may never overwrite newer authoritative state.
policy.rollback_rule: Rollback appends a governed event and moves the active pointer to the last proven compatible release bundle without rewriting project, release or evidence history.
policy.sculptural_kernel_rule: Plasma must not require a Parasolid-class exact-solid kernel to author or retain sculptural richness. Exact-solid kernels are used where constructive precision, booleans, interfaces, machining or fabrication require them; sculptural form may use subdivision, multiresolution mesh, sparse voxel/SDF, displacement, procedural or learned representations and is converted or wrapped into fabrication-valid geometry only where necessary.
policy.sculptural_separation_rule: Semantic identity, morphology/control structures, exact construction geometry, high-resolution sculptural surfaces and render-only microdetail are distinct state layers. High-poly surface vertices must not become the default dependency graph of the architectural object.
policy.self_modification_rule: Plasma never mutates an active authoritative capability in place. Candidate changes execute in a sandboxed branch, produce a new immutable capability version and replay affected project state on a separate branch.
policy.semantic_compilation_rule: Typed semantic state and dependencies may compile to sparse graphs/matrices, execution DAGs, transform matrices, Jacobians, tensor fields, meshes, B-Reps, USD and solver models for performance. These compiled forms are derived artefacts keyed to exact input revisions/producer versions and never replace semantic authority.
policy.semantic_sculpt_rule: AI and direct-manipulation sculpt operations should target semantic regions and morphological controls where possible (for example wing, head, vine branch, junction) rather than unstructured vertex identifiers, while permitting low-level surface editing when required.
policy.spectrum_status: research-only; not a prerequisite for Plasma Runtime
policy.standalone_proof_rule: This standalone HTML cannot authenticate independent collector provenance. Imported verification flags, test result files and localStorage records remain supporting evidence. Verified requires trusted provenance, exact matching source/artifact/input/evaluator/fixture scope, complete required-gate coverage, freshness and revocation checks through an independently governed collector.
policy.survey_proposal_ownership_rule: Survey evidence, editable ground controls, pad grading, driveway grading and derived contours/surfaces are distinct. The initial composition gives the pad authority inside its footprint; driveway grading modifies transition ground outside it. Source ground remains unchanged by design edits.
policy.transaction_semantics_rule: Canonical project mutation follows BEGIN → DECLARE → EXPAND → IMPACT → APPLY → DERIVE → EVALUATE → RESOLVE → COMMIT → EMIT. APPLY occurs in an isolated candidate world; COMMIT is atomic; hard conflicts block by default; unknown results follow explicit commit policy; rejection leaves the accepted world unchanged.
policy.transform_event_distinction_rule: Transform records what is proposed; Event records what actually happened. A rejected, failed or previewed Transform may produce an Event without producing a new accepted world revision.
policy.transform_only_mutation_rule: No human, agent, UI manipulator, solver, import or external engine may directly mutate accepted canonical state. All material mutation is expressed as typed Transform(s) executed inside a governed Transaction against an immutable base revision.
policy.unified_environment_rule: Architectural world state, reasoning, capability machinery, development work and evidence are presented as connected depths of one Plasma environment rather than separate products.
policy.unknowns_are_state_rule: Missing, conflicting, stale and low-confidence context are first-class world-state objects that propagate risk to dependent feasibility, cost, compliance, design and documentation outputs.
policy.vendor_sovereignty_rule: OpenUSD/Omniverse, NVIDIA runtimes, CAD kernels, renderers, solvers, AI models and other external ecosystems are replaceable capability providers. No vendor scene graph, mesh, solver state or model context becomes canonical owner of Plasma world identity, intent, evidence or transaction history.
policy.versioning_rule: Use SemVer to communicate compatibility for deployables, contracts, schemas, capabilities, agents and evaluators; use immutable revision/event/evidence IDs for world history; use content digests to establish exact identity.
policy.view_contract_rule: Each generated view explicitly carries purpose, storey/reference plane, direction, cut/projection/depth ranges, scale, semantic LOD, geometric LOD, discipline and graphic convention as applicable.
policy.work_item_truth_rule: WorkItem success means the declared output contract completed for pinned inputs; it does not imply truth, compliance, optimality or authorization. Results remain derived/proposed until evaluated and, where canonical mutation is required, committed through a governed transaction.
policy.work_orchestration_rule: Goals, events, Dirty Frontiers and information needs may compile into revision-pinned ExecutionPlans composed of typed WorkItems. Plans coordinate computation and human/machine activity but cannot directly mutate accepted world state or bypass PLS-KERNEL-01 publication semantics.
policy.work_publication_exactness_rule: Task execution may be at-least-once where safe; canonical publication is effectively exactly-once through idempotency plus optimistic-concurrency/transaction gates. External side effects require explicit dedupe, reconciliation and/or compensation semantics.
policy.work_scheduler_fairness_rule: PLS-15 scheduling reuses PLS-10 latency/currentness priorities, protects pointer and commit-critical paths from background saturation, cancels/discards superseded work and uses an explicit fairness/aging policy so valid lower-priority work cannot starve indefinitely.
policy.world_state_rule: Plasma distinguishes latest available state from latest mutually coherent state; accepted world revisions are immutable; State is attached to persistent Entity identity; Relations and Invariants are typed first-class records; derived results carry input revisions, producer/rule versions, parameters/tolerances and currentness.
